problem.claim: Gradient-based interpretations need a comparison anchor to avoid saturation when computing feature importance.

gap.claim: The authors argue that static baselines can impose harmful colour, texture, and frequency assumptions that diverge from model behaviour, producing biased, fragile, and manipulable attribution maps.

contributions.claim: UNI computes an adaptive, debiased baseline by perturbing the input toward an unlearning direction defined by steepest ascent.
The proposed approach uses unlearning to erase salient features and locally smooth high-curvature decision boundaries.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish UNI from static-baseline approaches by making the baseline adaptive and unlearning-based.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that UNI discovers reliable baselines and succeeds in erasing salient features, with corresponding local smoothing of high-curvature decision boundaries.
The authors report analyses indicating that unlearning is promising for faithful, efficient, and robust interpretations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Gradient-based interpretation methods require an anchor to mitigate saturation in feature-importance computation.
The authors attribute failures of static baselines to injected colour, texture, and frequency assumptions, which accumulate irregular gradients.
UNI replaces the static approach with an adaptive baseline obtained by perturbing inputs along an unlearning direction.
The authors report reliable baselines, salient-feature erasure, and local smoothing of high-curvature boundaries.
The analyses frame unlearning as a promising route to faithful, efficient, and robust interpretations.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a concrete baseline design choice to specific failure modes—assumption mismatch, irregular gradients, and biased or manipulable attribution maps—before presenting an adaptive alternative.

lessons.interpretation: This creates a traceable chain from mechanism to pathology to intervention.
lessons.application: When proposing an interpretation method, explicitly connect the design choice to the failure mode it is intended to address and state the intermediate mechanism.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the failure mechanism has not been established or when the method targets a different objective.

unknowns: The abstract gives no datasets, quantitative metrics, baselines, or experimental conditions for the reported outcomes.
It does not specify how reliability, faithfulness, efficiency, robustness, or local boundary smoothing are operationalized.
The abstract does not provide comparative evidence establishing superiority over existing methods.
